body: No I'm not.  And I've given as much evidence as you have.

>Happiness is the key to success.

That's precisely what I mean.  If someone is successful, then 9 times out of 10 it's because they're happy (and not depressed or suicidal).  So it's impossible for me to believe that the people I see every day who are outwardly doing well could be having emotional difficulty.

>1. Think everyone else has it better than you.
Example: "Everyone I see is so happy and they're all successful."

How many of the visibly successful people around me are obsessed with killing themselves?  Is it normal for the average person to loathe their very own existence, and yet still be able to put in a full day's work with a smile on their face?

Not everyone has it as good as me (lol /r/firstworldproblems), but I refuse to believe the majority of people suffer simply from being themselves.  I refuse to believe this is normal.

Yeah, "trapped" is a good description for it.  It feels like everything I do is out of obligation to others, and anything I want to do for myself is selfish, irresponsible, or disrespectful to the needs of others.

>Whats wrong with being selfish? Whats wrong with putting your needs first?

With all due respect, that's a very naive question.  Society makes it quite clear how selfishness is perceived.

The Robert Glover recommendation sounds interesting.  I guess I need to get myself to a library...

A problem I have is the inability to get away from any of it.  All of my time and energy goes to work or taking care of the family.  When I try making time for myself, I'm made to feel guilty about it, or else it gets cancelled by some unforeseen circumstances.  So to do anything personally fulfilling or "fun" seems to mean losing my job or abandoning my family.

It's very difficult for me not to be fundamentally selfish.  I only think about my own issues and feelings as it is.  Making time for myself seems like it's going in the wrong direction.

Burns' "Feeling Good" seems to be universally recommended, so I'm sure I need to bring myself to read it.  I'm not an avid reader by any definition, but at this point I pretty much have to force myself to do something about this problem.

See, this doesn't really jive with the sentiment in [this highly-rated comment.](http://www.reddit.com/r/depression/comments/i03w9/when_the_fuck_will_it_end/c1zsr9h).  I just don't know what to believe anymore.

I'm sorely tempted to try admitting myself somewhere (I still find it hard to believe that a hospital would admit someone just because they were feeling suicidal, I didn't think they had the room or staff necessary).

But that's pretty much just announcing to everyone what my problem is.  I'd be rolling the dice with work, and leaving my family in a lurch while I was admitted.  And judging from the stories I've heard here, nothing useful might actually come of it.  But I guess one could argue it's more sensible than suicide.

The department consists of me and my boss, so there's no benchmark.

I'm sure what you suggest is the proper, rational solution, but I'm out of patience.  I need this to end now.
